technique.summary: Access other users' resources by manipulating object IDs in API requests. Even UUID-based IDs can be predictable (v1 UUIDs are time-based) or leaked through other endpoints. BOLA is the #1 OWASP API risk.
steps: Identify API endpoints that reference objects by ID (users, orders, documents)
Create two test accounts and obtain valid object IDs for each
Using Account A's session, try accessing Account B's resources by changing the ID
Test both direct URL path IDs and request body IDs
If sequential IDs: enumerate by incrementing/decrementing
If UUID v1: extract timestamp component and generate likely UUIDs
Check if the API returns different errors for 'not found' vs 'forbidden' (info leak)

payloads.notes: UUID-based IDOR — find UUIDs from other endpoints or email notifications
IDOR in request body — different from URL-based

bypassTechniques: UUID v1 prediction: extract timestamp, generate adjacent UUIDs
Find ID leaks in: API list endpoints, email links, Referer headers, JS files
Try accessing via different HTTP methods (GET vs POST vs PUT)
Try both numeric and string versions: /users/1 vs /users/00001
Check if GraphQL queries have different authorization than REST endpoints
Test nested resource access: /users/1/orders (may bypass authorization on /orders/X)
